seasonMovement: Impossible arrival -> settlement -> navigation -> participation -> belonging -> usefulness -> chosen household -> self-defined belonging under judgment.
seasonDramaticShift: Issues 1–5 are driven largely by collision with 2026 and the work of building an ordinary life. From Issue 6 forward, modern systems remain real pressure but stop being the default dramatic protagonist. The later season is driven by what these particular people want from work, one another, New York, autonomy, responsibility, and belonging.

kinContinuity.composition: Two men and Astrid, the only woman.
kinContinuity.issues1To3: The three Kin are seen primarily together in or immediately around the Bushwick placement; they are not yet followed independently around the city.
kinContinuity.middleSeason: Their independent errands, relationships, routines and interests begin to appear individually.
kinContinuity.issues6To7: Astrid is deliberately largely absent from foreground action while the two male Kin remain visible. Her absence is ordinary, not mysterious.
kinContinuity.issue8: The hearing reveals that Astrid has quietly become the household's most practically integrated member.
kinContinuity.maleNames: Personal names remain unresolved and intentionally unlettered through Issues 7–8. Current production identities are First Male Kin / @vik.KinMan1 and Second Male Kin / @vik.KinMan2; this does not block production.

issues.title: Landfall Bushwick
issues.function: Apartment adaptation and neighborhood integration; food, neighbors, domestic choice and privacy make the temporary shelter into a functioning household while the acknowledgement problem remains a bounded threat underneath the story.

issues.title: The Tally of Dishonor
issues.function: Financial legibility, value and partial civic participation; the bank is resolved in the first act, then money becomes household choice, reciprocal debt, neighborhood exchange and ordinary capability.
issues.status: structural season revision complete; 24-page revised script compiled; dialogue line-polish pending

issues.title: The Skaldic Interface
issues.function: Neighborhood-memory and emerging belonging; recurring relationships and ordinary routines show the Vikings beginning to live independently in New York. This is where the three Kin begin to read as separate people rather than a permanent background unit.
issues.status: production-ready 24-page enhanced script encoded in RexPrompt; visual recipes normalized with panel-level location

issues.title: Trial of Toil
issues.function: Bjorn's crisis over usefulness becomes a character story about respect, consent, responsibility and meaningful contribution. The support group changes his behavior, but the revised middle tests that change through distinct situations—emergency action, shared household obligation, ordinary belonging, difficult advice, emotional witnessing and trust—rather than repeated requested-help exercises.
issues.status: structural tightening complete; active 24-page RexPrompt payload updated; dialogue line-polish pending

issues.title: War Council
issues.function: A Status Reconciliation Review forces the household to confront different wants without reducing them to one household doctrine. The city excursions make those wants concrete; the final council prepares five people to answer for themselves while leaving permanence, kinship, integration and Astrid's practical competence for the hearing to discover.
issues.status: Issue 8 discovery-preservation pass complete; active 24-page RexPrompt payload updated; dialogue line-polish pending

issues.title: Permanent Residency / Trial by Combat
issues.function: The hearing tests whether an institution can make a fair decision about a real but unconventional household made of separate people. Bjorn's trial is allowing others to speak for themselves; Astrid's payoff is the revelation that the least-followed member has quietly become the most practically integrated.

finaleState.ordeal: Issue 8 residency hearing functions as Bjorn's trial by combat without literal combat.
finaleState.hearingPurpose: The institution encounters a household that cannot honestly be reduced to one spokesperson, one integration narrative, or one permanent future.
finaleState.bjorn: Bjorn arrives in armor without weapons. His growth is visible when he answers for himself and protects other people's right to speak and choose instead of speaking over them.
finaleState.carrie: Carrie does not ask him to remove the armor. Her strongest testimony acknowledges that successful integration means she increasingly does not know every detail of the household's life.
finaleState.astrid: Astrid's ordinary independent competence becomes visible in court and reveals that the background member Carrie and Bjorn tracked least is the household's most practically integrated person.
